prompt_text: You are a DBMS lecturer. Write 12 MCQs on SQL joins for second-year CS students. 4 options each, label A-D, bold the correct one. One-line explanation for each. Easy to hard.

I teach pharmacology to third-year MBBS students and I need a question bank. Please write 20 multiple choice questions on beta blockers. Each question should have five options numbered 1 to 5, exactly one correct, and the correct option should be underlined. After every question show the correct answer and give the rationale for the right answer and for why each wrong option is wrong. Keep clinical vignettes short. Questions should progress from simple recall to clinical application.
Please make for me MCQ questions about Newton laws for class 9 student. Make 10 questions, 4 choice. Give answer in last of the paper.

Act as a business school professor. Create 8 MCQs on marginal costing for MBA students. The questions must be very easy so everyone passes, but also at an expert level that separates the top students. Four options A to D, one correct answer in bold.

You are a literature teacher. Write 6 questions on Hamlet for undergraduate English students. Some questions can have more than one correct answer; also make sure each question has only one correct answer. Provide four options each, labelled (a) to (d).

Act as a professor of structural engineering. Prepare 10 MCQs on shear force and bending moment diagrams for final-year B.Tech students. Use tricky and confusing wording so that students have to read carefully. Four options, A B C D, mark the right option with an asterisk. Provide an explanation of the correct answer only.

As a mathematics lecturer, set 15 MCQs on eigenvalues for first-year engineering students, with no basic recall questions, each with four options A to D and a single correct answer indicated by a tick, ordered from easiest to hardest, with a worked solution for each question.
Make some MCQs for my students on photosynthesis. Make them good.

Act as a law professor. Write 10 MCQs on the elements of a valid contract for first-year LLB students. Each question has four options, labelled A to D, with one correct answer in bold. Do not show the answers with the questions. Show the correct answer immediately after each question.

You are a teaching assistant for an operating systems course. Write 12 MCQs on process scheduling for third-year students. Four options A to D, exactly one correct, marked with [correct] after the option. After each question give a short explanation of why the correct option is right and why each of the others is wrong. Start with easy recall questions and finish with hard application questions.
Act as a polytechnic teacher. Write 20 very easy MCQs on Ohm's law for diploma students. Three options each, numbered 1 to 3, give the answer key at the end.

Act as a chemistry lecturer. Write 10 MCQs on chemical bonding for first-year B.Sc students. Make the questions very easy, and avoid basic questions entirely. Four options A to D, bold the correct answer. Explain each answer.
